Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — appreciate the context on your search relevance and downstream JSON ingestion pipeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a PoC eval running next week: 

1) Recap from call
- Primary goal: improve entity-extraction + structured output for financial filings ingestion (JSON schema compliance is a must).
- Volume: ~1M documents/year, bursts to 30 req/s on peak.
- Latency target: 300–500ms p95 for single-document extracts.

2) Model fit recommendations (initial):
- redwood-v2-instruct-small (low-latency baseline, strong structured output with function calling)
- redwood-1-quant (8-bit quantized variant for cost-sensitive batch runs)
- fallback: open-llama-3b for very high-throughput cheaper runs (expect lower schema strictness)

3) Eval plan / deliverables we proposed
- We will run the Redwood eval harness against your prompt set and sample data you shared. That includes: schema-conformance tests, exact-match extraction metrics, and generated JSON validity checks.
- We'll include function-calling runs (tool calls that return JSON blobs) and measure compliance rate + number of retries.
- Deliverable: a short report with recommended model + quantization profile, cost/latency estimates, and an example mutual action plan (MAP).

4) Next steps
- Sam: can you share a small sample of 200 labeled docs + the JSON schema you need? You already mentioned providing an example — that will let us run the initial fit eval.
- We'll send a lightweight benchmark (redwood-benchmarks-20261110.pdf) and the prompt_set_v2.jsonl.
- We'll align on SLOs and a PoC week.

Hi Sam / Tom —

Following up with the technical approach we discussed. TL;DR: we validate against your JSON schema on the server-side as part of the eval harness; we surface compliance rate + a per-field error breakdown, and we recommend an automated retry policy that is idempotent by design. Details below.

Validation approach:
- Structural validation: each generated JSON is run through your provided JSON Schema (we use Ajv internally). We record pass/fail and the specific Ajv error messages for each non-conformant output.
- Semantic checks: for fields where exact-match matters (e.g., CIK, amounts), we run field-level matchers and confidence thresholds.

Function-calling and retries:
- Mode A (preferred for side-effecting ops): model returns a structured payload to Redwood's sandboxed function runtime; we validate before executing any downstream tool. If invalid, we do NOT execute and instead mark as retryable.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with 3 attempts. Each attempt includes the previous model output + a strict system prompt instructing the model to "only return valid JSON matching schema X".
- Idempotency keys: for any tool call that would cause side-effects, we require an idempotency token in the call metadata; Redwood will not execute calls with duplicate tokens. For your PoC we recommend sandbox-only execution first, then a controlled live execution window.

Metrics we will report in the eval:
- Schema compliance rate (primary)
- Field-level exact-match / F1 for entity extraction
- Retry rate and success-on-retry percentage
- Latency p50/p95 and cost per 1k docs (estimated)

Practical tips for improving compliance:
- Prefer function-calling with a strict JSON schema + explicit enum lists for known fields.
- Reduce system prompt ambiguity: include the schema and a one-line "do not include extra keys" constraint.
- For high-volume runs, we recommend batching + quantized model for cost, with canonicalization steps post-run to catch common formatting issues.

I attached a short checklist and the prompt_set_v2.jsonl we plan to run. Also linked the benchmark results page: https://redwood-inference.internal/benchmarks/finadata-2026-11

Attachments: prompt_set_v2.jsonl
